agriculture.safe_framing: Highest average corn yields of any Ohio county; 96% of soils prime or locally important. Do NOT claim top-tier land prices.

county_unemployment_rate.note: Below Ohio's 3.3% in Sept 2026. This is NOT a distressed labor market.

wilmington_lodes_wac_jobs.note: 56% of all county jobs on 1.9x its resident worker count

construction_workforce.note: 3.8x spread. Clinton is rural: many self-employed trades (ACS sees them, CBP/QCEW do not) and few construction firms payrolled in-county. Prefer QCEW for workplace baseline.

commute_shed.note: CRITICAL: 62.9% of Clinton jobs are already held by in-commuters across the Cincinnati-Dayton-Columbus triangle. Model labor supply and housing demand on the SHED, not the town. A 6.3% local vacancy rate does NOT imply a housing crunch.

dhl_natural_experiment._note: Calibrates how this county absorbs a large employment shock. The direction nobody else has data for.

couriers_naics492_peak.note: The hub itself. Fell to 173 by 2010, 20-99 by 2011, absent after 2016.

dhl_natural_experiment.headline: The job base fell 43-49% while population fell 2.0%. Adjustment ran through labor-force exit and out-commuting, NOT migration. Expect the same asymmetry on the upside: a job boom will not mechanically add population.
data_traps: LAUS 2015->2016 jumps +21% employed in one year â€” a re-benchmarking artifact, not recovery. QCEW over the same span moves only 15,873 -> 16,813.
Per-capita income ROSE through the collapse because transfer payments masked it. Income is useless as a shock detector.
CBP changed regimes in 2018: pre-2018 uses empflag suppression (emp=0), 2018+ uses noise infusion. Parsing both the same way SILENTLY ZEROES OUT the DHL hub.
2008 Transportation-48 is suppressed at [10k-25k], so the true transport peak may be 2008 rather than 2007.
